_note: The two abilities you pick on landing (battle royale) or at the first countdown (1v1v1, bots). Names are ours. JOLT's distance, its two charges and the 4 s a charge takes to come back (8 s for both) are the owner's numbers; its duration, the gap between two dashes and the exit speed are ours. TRIAGE's scale is the owner's (twice as fast = every heal item's use time halved).

jolt.name: JOLT
jolt.blurb: dash 10 m the way you are moving; two charges, one back every 4 s
jolt._gap: the least time from one dash's start to the next, so two cannot merge into one 20 m teleport (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_12.md section 6)
jolt._exit: you leave a dash at this speed the way it went (400 hu/s, 10 m/s, the slide cap; above the 260 sprint), so it carries into a slide or a jump; friction takes it down from there. The dash itself is an ease-out: 70% of the distance in the first half
jolt._feel: the view on a dash: the FOV kick in degrees, a roll toward the side you went (degrees, rising in rollIn s, back over rollOut s), a pad rumble (strong, weak, ms)

triage.name: TRIAGE
triage.blurb: every heal works twice as fast

bots._note: ours: a JOLT bot jolts sideways when it has been hit in the last `joltWhenHitWithin` seconds; every bot heals when it has had no target for `healAfter` seconds. A SMOKE bot throws a cloud between itself and whoever is shooting it once it is under `coverAtHealth` of its health, and a WARD bot puts a wall up in the same spot in the same case; neither does it more often than `coverGap` seconds, and neither does it at all further than `coverRange` metres, where a cloud or a wall is cover for the other side as much as for itself. A bot's cover is meant to make a fight read, not to make a bot unkillable: it breaks the line of sight it is already losing and then it moves.
